title: TC-01 Regex entry grants Team to matching subgroups, including a new one (AC-1)
precondition:
- OIDC provider with Regex entry app-team-.* mapped to Team X, mode roles_teams.
- Three test users in the IdP, in groups app-team-frontend, app-team-backend and none of them yet in app-team-security.
steps:
[1] Log in as the user in group app-team-frontend

[2] Log in as the user in group app-team-backend

[3] On the IdP, create group app-team-security, add the third user, then log in without changing anything in Horizon
expected_results:
[1] Login succeeds; the user is a member of Team X

[2] The user is a member of Team X

[3] The user is a member of Team X

title: TC-02 Matching rules: whole value, case sensitivity, inline flag (AC-4)
precondition:
- Regex entries: team-.* -> Team Y, App-Team-.* -> Team X, (?i)ops-.* -> Team Z, app-team -> Team W.
- One test user per claim value below.
steps:
[1] Log in with claim value x-team-frontend

[2] Log in with claim value team-frontend

[3] Log in with claim value app-team-frontend

[4] Log in with claim value App-Team-frontend

[5] Log in with claim value OPS-Frontend
expected_results:
[1] Team Y is not granted (no substring match)

[2] Team Y is granted

[3] Team X is not granted (case-sensitive) and Team W is not granted (trailing characters)

[4] Team X is granted

[5] Team Z is granted (inline flag (?i))

title: TC-03 Static and Regex entries coexist, union of Roles and Teams (AC-3)
precondition:
- Static entry admin -> Role A.
- Regex entries admin.* -> Role B and .*-backend -> Team Y.
- Static entry app-.* -> Team Z (regex characters must be literal).
steps:
[1] Log in with claim value admin

[2] Log in with claim value admin2

[3] Log in with claim values admin and app-backend

[4] Log in with claim value app-frontend, then with the literal value app-.*

[5] Log in with claim value marketing
expected_results:
[1] The user holds Role A and Role B

[2] The user holds Role B only (static entry is an exact match)

[3] The user holds Role A, Role B and Team Y (union across entries)

[4] Team Z is not granted for app-frontend (static, literal); Team Z is granted for the literal value

[5] No Role or Team is granted by the mapping

title: TC-04 Invalid regex is rejected on save (UI and API) (AC-2)
precondition:
- OIDC provider edit page open, valid configuration saved beforehand.
- API credentials of a Business administrator.
steps:
[1] In the UI, add a Regex entry with value app-team-[ and Team X, then save

[2] Reload the provider

[3] Add a valid Regex entry app-team-.* then an invalid one (admin (second entry), and save

[4] Send the same invalid pattern through the provider update API

[5] Add a Regex entry with an empty value and save [needs clarification]
expected_results:
[1] Save is blocked with an error that names the offending entry

[2] The invalid entry is not persisted; the previous configuration is unchanged

[3] The error designates the second entry, not the first

[4] Request is rejected with a client error naming the entry; configuration unchanged

[5] Behaviour to be defined: rejection or acceptance (Open Question 2)

title: TC-05 Reference rules on Roles and Teams still apply to Regex entries (FR-7)
precondition:
- API credentials of a Business administrator.
- Role ghost-role and Team ghost-team do not exist.
- Role A and Team X exist.
steps:
[1] Update the provider with Regex entry app-.* targeting ghost-role

[2] Update the provider with Regex entry app-.* targeting ghost-team

[3] Update the provider with Regex entry app-.* with neither Role nor Team

[4] Set mode roles and add a Regex entry targeting Team X

[5] Save a valid Regex entry app-.* -> Role A and Team X, then try to delete Role A and Team X
expected_results:
[1] Rejected: Role(s) referenced in claim mapping do not exist

[2] Rejected: Team(s) referenced in claim mapping do not exist

[3] Rejected: an entry must contain at least one role or team

[4] Rejected: entries must not reference teams when the mode is roles

[5] Both deletions are refused because they are referenced by the OIDC claim mapping

title: TC-06 Match type control in the UI (FR-1, NFR-4, FR-3)
precondition: - Business administrator logged in, expert mode disabled, OIDC provider edit page open with one Static entry app-team-.* -> Team X.
steps:
[1] Add a new claim mapping entry

[2] Select Regex on the new entry

[3] Save, reload the page

[4] Switch the first entry from Static to Regex, save, and log in with app-team-frontend
expected_results:
[1] Match type is preselected to Static; the control is visible outside expert mode

[2] Helper text explains the value is a regular expression and shows an example such as app-team-.*

[3] The entry keeps the Regex match type and its value

[4] Team X is granted; with the entry set back to Static, it is not

title: TC-07 Synchronization modes apply to Regex entries (NFR-5, FR-2)
precondition:
- Regex entry app-.* -> Role A and Team X.
- Test user already holding Role B and Team Z (set manually).
steps:
[1] Set mode roles, log in with claim app-frontend

[2] Set mode teams, log in with the same claim

[3] Set mode roles_teams, log in with the same claim, then remove the user from the IdP group and log in again
expected_results:
[1] Role A granted; Team X not granted; Team Z kept

[2] Team X granted; Role B kept

[3] After the first login the user has Role A and Team X; after the second the mapped Roles and Teams are removed (Replace)

title: TC-08 Existing mappings unchanged after upgrade, and old exports import as Static (AC-5)
precondition: - Horizon 2.10 or 2.11 with exact-match entries (admin -> Role A, finance -> Team Y) and a configuration export from that version, then upgrade to 2.12.0.
steps:
[1] After the upgrade, open the claim mapping

[2] Log in with claims admin and finance

[3] Import the old configuration export into a clean 2.12.0 tenant
expected_results:
[1] Every existing entry shows Match type Static; values and targets unchanged

[2] Role A and Team Y are granted exactly as before the upgrade

[3] Import succeeds; all entries are Static

title: TC-09 Configuration export and import preserve Regex entries (FR-8)
precondition:
- Provider with one Static and one Regex entry (app-team-.* -> Team X).
- A clean target tenant.
steps:
[1] Export the configuration

[2] Import the export into the clean tenant

[3] Open the provider and log in with app-team-frontend
expected_results:
[1] The OIDC Identity Provider contains the match type of both entries, Regex marked as such

[2] Import succeeds

[3] The Regex entry is present and effective; Team X is granted

title: TC-10 Access control on claim mapping configuration (ACT-1)
precondition: - One user with the Identity Provider management permission, one without.
steps:
[1] As the authorized user, add and save a Regex entry (UI)

[2] As the other user, open the identity provider page and send an update with a Regex entry via the API

[3] Compare the permission list with 2.11
expected_results:
[1] Save succeeds

[2] Edition is not possible in the UI; the API refuses the request

[3] No permission related to claim mapping or regex has been added

title: TC-11 Audit event on save (NFR-3)
steps:
[1] Save the provider with a Regex entry

[2] Look for any new event type tied to the action
expected_results:
[1] One SEC-IDENTITY-PROVIDER-UPDATE event is recorded

[2] No new event type exists

title: TC-12 Claim mapping is isolated per tenant (NFR-4)
precondition: - Two tenants; tenant A has Regex entry app-.* -> Team X, tenant B has none.
steps:
[1] As root tenant administrator, open the provider of each tenant

[2] Log in on tenant B with claim app-frontend
expected_results:
[1] Each tenant shows only its own entries

[2] Team X is not granted

title: TC-14 Pathological regex and many entries do not degrade login (NFR-2)

- Regex entry (a+)+$ saved (acceptance by validation is itself unspecified).
- A provider variant with 100 Regex entries and a user with 50 group values.
steps:
[1] Log in with a claim of 40 characters a followed by !

[2] Measure login time on the 100-entry provider, and compare with 100 Static entries
expected_results:
[1] Login ends within a bounded time and the server stays responsive; exact limit to define (Open Question 1)

[2] The difference is acceptable; threshold to be defined by the team
